note: PLACEHOLDER. Every params object here validates against the published trending_issues manifest input_schema (additionalProperties: false, $refs inlined the way publish_experiments.py inlines them), and every value is plausible, but nobody has dispatched one. So a verdict drawn from this list is a claim about the pipeline, not about the agent. EIGHT cases, and DEFAULT_JUDGE_CONFIG.gates.minCases is 20. A corpus verdict over this list therefore resolves CAN'T SAY however the judge voted, because the floor was set from measured agent non-determinism and eight runs measure that rather than the branch. Eight is deliberate and not a rounding error: one clean baseline plus seven single-axis variations is what one change can author honestly. Whether to grow every list to 20 or to lower the floor is still open — do not read the shortfall as a decision. {judgeOrgSlug} is not a value: they are substituted at dispatch time from the per-sweep test fixture in sweepFixture.ts, and assertNoPlaceholders refuses the whole list before the first dispatch if a sweep did not supply one. A literal slug cannot be written here, because the only supported way to get a dev organization in a known state is POST /v1/test-fixtures/users and those users are swept after about 24 hours — so a hardcoded one is right for a day and then makes every later sweep read as an agent failure. The organization is therefore the one axis this list cannot vary, and here it is load-bearing rather than decorative: step 2 reads the current issue feed with GET_community_issues scoped to this slug so carried issues keep their existing IDs, which is a real lookup against a real elected office. The fixture's org is a fresh one, so that read returns an empty feed on both arms, identically, which is the property a comparison needs even though it leaves the carry-forward path unexercised. Varied along: the four fields are all this agent takes, so the axis is the district itself and how much local reporting exists to surge: a Minneapolis ward and an at-large Oakland seat sit in dense daily coverage, a Fayetteville or Dover ward in one paper's municipal beat, and a Flathead county district or a Bellefonte borough ward in a weekly with no archive — which is the case where 'trending this week' has the least to draw on; district geometry, from a named ward to a bare district number to a whole jurisdiction; and one non-municipal body, a school board, whose coverage is a different corpus from a council's. People are fictional placeholders in the house style (gp-webapp e2e-tests briefings.spec.ts uses 'Test Official'); this file is public, so no real person is named and every URL is under example.org. States, cities, office titles and L2 voter file column names are real.
